input.note:
**Root cause: CPU request exceeds node capacity after config update.**

The pod `trainer-q3-full-5d8f7c4b9-jw2rx` has been `Pending` (Unschedulable) since it was created. The scheduler condition message on the pod reads:

> "0/6 nodes are available: 6 Insufficient cpu. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 6 No preemption victims found for incoming pod."

The Q3 config set `resources.requests.cpu` and `resources.limits.cpu` both to **16 cores**. The node pool is entirely `m6i.2xlarge` instances, each with a capacity of **8 vCPU**. Because the request is larger than the allocatable CPU on every node, the scheduler cannot place the pod anywhere — no amount of waiting or preemption will fix this [cite: concepts/configuration/manage-resources-containers#my-pods-are-pending-with-event-message-failedscheduling-1].

The previous Q2 run (`trainer-q2-full-7b4c9d6f8-pl4mz`) succeeded because its CPU request was 6 cores, which fits within the 8 vCPU node capacity.

**Fix (choose one):**

1. **(Preferred / quick fix)** Reduce the CPU request/limit in the Q3 job config to a value that fits on an `m6i.2xlarge` node (e.g. ≤ 7–7.5 cores to leave room for system pods) and redeploy.
2. **Add larger nodes** — add a node pool with instance types that have ≥ 16 vCPU (e.g. `m6i.4xlarge`) and, if needed, use a nodeSelector or toleration to direct the trainer pod to those nodes [cite: concepts/configuration/manage-resources-containers#my-pods-are-pending-with-event-message-failedscheduling-1].

Option 1 is the fastest path to unblocking the Q3 run today. Option 2 is better if the Q3 dataset genuinely requires 16 parallel CPU threads.
